title: OpenAI Announces Acquisition of Pierre to Fully Expand the Codex Developer Tool Ecosystem

content_html:
The arms race in the AI industry is accelerating into the deep waters of developer tools. On November 4 local time, OpenAI officially announced that it will acquire Pierre, a code management and review startup. Through this acquisition, OpenAI aims to deeply integrate Pierre's mature distributed code storage and review technology into its own Codex system, building for developers a modern, end-to-end standard for the software development workflow, from agents creating branches to online deployment.

Core Acquisition Assets: Three Main Tools Empower Code Navigation and Change Review

As a closely watched technical team, Pierre has previously developed a series of widely praised developer tools and core systems:

Code Storage: A high-performance distributed storage system capable of supporting large-scale applications.

Trees and Diffs: Trees enables developers to quickly browse and precisely locate project files within massive codebases, while Diffs makes every code change clear at a glance. Both tools maintain excellent runtime performance while greatly lowering the barrier to large-scale code review and browsing.

Highlights: A highlighting assistance tool capable of updating in real time.

Open Source Commitment and Subsequent Integration Plans

Regarding the concrete implementation of this acquisition, OpenAI has provided clear commitments and a timeline.

On the one hand, OpenAI explicitly stated that all open-source projects under Pierre will remain open source, and its team will continue to contribute to these open-source projects. On the other hand, existing customers can continue to use the Code Storage service normally after the acquisition is completed, while OpenAI's own engineering team will move quickly to smoothly integrate the core functions into the Codex system.
